notes: Single author; paired McNemar tests with Wilson intervals, cross-day and cross-hardware reproducibility, held-out threshold splits (500); self-audit corrected four headline errors; safety gold LLM-made (agrees with dataset labels 72.8%); multilingual cells n=10; no multiplicity correction.

Benchmark by ufak AI whose own typed model is on the board (flagged as not blind); Jev, Kev, Laya, open-jev are third-party; gold mostly AI-made by one model family, one human annotator; bootstrap intervals likely too narrow on LLM-written tracks; Turkish data; per-track moderation and guardrail scores only in board file.

Authors build the typed models (sbert2s1) and compare fine-tuned Laya-large and two zero-shot LLMs; 3 seeds, cluster bootstrap with Holm correction; held-out task family; routing budget fixed retrospectively on test; minor train-test duplicates; hosted Jev not measured.

Third-party analysis of open laya and von checkpoints with an intervention on prompt rendering; synthetic templated PolicyBench (n=3,500) plus 11 public tasks; paired bootstrap intervals; Jev itself not measured; option definitions written by the authors.

Authors build and release SecJev on Kev; grouped train/calibration/development/test splits with source-stratified bootstrap intervals; one training run per condition; transfer sets small (150 BIPIA contexts, 4 IoT-23 captures); hosted Jev not measured.

Independent evaluation of hosted Jev and five open decision models on full test sets of four English hate-speech datasets; group bootstrap with Bonferroni-adjusted intervals; definitions and decomposition rules are the authors' operationalisation (proxy for HateXplain); prior data exposure unknown; routing analysis exploratory.

v2 read; fixed calibration and test splits with text-bootstrap intervals; small natural-miss populations (31, 11 and 5 queries) and 20-text controls; one version per model; Qwen gives discrete choices only, so score-based policies cover Laya and Jev only.

Jev was queried by API on JEVal samples (at most 200 per subtask from test or validation splits). Generative LLMs were run once at temperature 1.0, with no intervals except Wilson intervals for long context. The tau-bench run was single and its text and Table 3 disagree (overall pass 64.2% in the text vs 66.1% in the table; P95 1,009.5 s vs 816.0 s). The election simulation uses the authors' own InnerJev-27B (author-built); the hosted-Jev election runs are preliminary and not tabulated.
30 synthetic instances per wireless task, run once, no intervals. Edge-orchestration figures are redrawn from another paper. No calibration, escalation or detection measured. Context tier.

Attack and test states were generated by GPT-4o (200 per task). Results are means of three runs, without intervals. Detection used separate calibration and test splits. NanoJev is a third-party open model (Eve-RLCD). The misuse demonstrations (App. C) are scored by a Llama-3-8B judge. The GPT-6 privacy comparison is qualitative (10 facts).

SearchJev and SearchDecision-Bench are the authors' own (Huawei). ID and OOD splits are held out; no intervals are reported. The end-to-end agent was run once on 100 sampled questions, and the gate threshold cannot be recovered from the logs. LLMs helped label 33.7% of training rows.
Graph-task capability benchmark with single executions and unadjusted paired bootstrap intervals. 1,186 of 6,684 Jev probability vectors in the public reports did not sum to one. Context tier.

SoK with bounded measurements: one random stream per experiment, exploratory questions formulated after the records were inspected, Holm correction within families, and constructed application tasks. Edge and RAN data are reused from the authors' own earlier studies of Jev, which they did not build.

Seven published human-coded benchmarks. Jev, GPT-6 Luna and Qwen3.8-27B were run once, with paired bootstrap intervals; test-retest replays were done for Jev only. The recall tasks (party positions, V-Dem) may reflect recall of the benchmarks from training data.

The author's own open model, scored on the author's own benchmark (HakemBench), with three seeds per recipe and bootstrap intervals. The released run's guardrail, moderation and support numbers were shaped by reading test results. One human annotator; most gold labels were set by LLM passes; some legal and guardrail items are in-distribution for this model only.

Preregistration frozen before any item was scored (two declared departures: hosted strong judge, duplicate-id handling); CLM and laya are third-party open models; laya's 512-token window truncates most items on four benchmarks; latency-cost criterion not evaluated; benchmark labels not adjudicated.

Microsoft authors evaluate their own SharedKV-BT (Jev-style readout on Qwen2.5-3B); simulated robot tasks plus three computer-use tasks; 120 replayed states repeat across seeds so counts are descriptive; ABSTAIN test n=60; intervals only for latency.

Seven third-party open typed families (kev, Open-Jev, decider, this-that, Mica, Tiny-Jev); 91 menu interventions; held-out CLINC150 splits for cascade and label repair; one sign test (p=0.016), otherwise no intervals; hosted Jev not measured.

SanSi is the authors' model; three seeds and bootstrap intervals over item groups; 10,027 English test items; Jev API is a single-run reference that was not trained to output a uniform distribution on unanswerable items.

Jev v1.13 and Laya v0.3 tested by independent authors; leave-one-out and official-split held-out retrieval; bootstrap CIs not adjusted for multiplicity; GPT-5.2, Detoxify and published systems are non-matched external references; English only; ModerationBench adapted to text with generated captions.
Formal database-theory paper; simulations on a synthetic workload in which calibration holds by construction; no typed model measured; evaluation on real engines left for future work.
Authors' S1-MAS with third-party Laya as coordination controller and GPT-4o workers; three seeds with standard deviations, no intervals or tests; context tier, no requirement coded.

Original release endpoint prospectively specified; verifier predicate, relaxed numeric baseline and column intervention post hoc; natural-record labels from unblinded assistant review; fresh 36-page bank with one blinded non-author reviewer; constructed contrast sets small (15, 7 and 36 pairs).

Jev is a side comparator on the same uniform 1,000-instance samples as the zero-shot LLMs (single pass, no interval for Jev); generative zero-shot RAID scores only in Fig. 2; costs are projections at $0.042/M input tokens.

Hosted jev-1.13.0 used zero-shot directly and inside the authors' training-free Emo-Jev procedures; one run per configuration, no intervals or tests; HD test set n=50; Chinese CMMA dataset; LLMs given Chinese or English instructions by model; some retry costs missing.

Game-split held-out pairs, fresh openings and bootstrap intervals for chess; five seeds for reranking; Jev is a label source for distilled evaluators, so most results test the evaluators, not live Jev decisions; Jev version not reported.
Authors' Qwen3.5-4B Jev-style verifier; one GRPO run per reward; 21-task human validation with bootstrap CI crossing zero; GPT-5.4 used for question construction, annotation and downstream scoring.

900 held-out questions from unseen seeds with game-resampled CIs; actor and rate re-selected over 500 held-out game splits; closed loop is a 33-game case study (3 seeds per variant); author's own doomGemma is a reference, not coded; oracle labels encode one policy.

Chip is the authors' Kev-0.8B fine-tune evaluated on a held-out test subset (SDDBench, 5,000 records); single run, no intervals; Chinese-language requests generated by seven LLMs; JEV version not reported; JevBench reference rows taken from a public table.

Nine shift tests with day-resampled CIs; wording frozen and hashed before scoring; three repeat passes for Jev; author declares no TypeSafe relationship; few fault days per type and one building pair for the building shift.

Probability samples with out-of-fold recalibration and a design-based second human tier drawn after estimates were fixed (specialist kappa 0.93); same authors and reuses the wave-1 reads and phase-2 human tier of arx24052, so not independent evidence from that study.
Jev as featurizer only (probabilities never thresholded); preregistration with dated amendment log; G3 numbers corrected in v1.1.0 after a thread-race defect; single author, no outside replication.
Laya (third-party open model) used zero-shot inside the author's agent; 3 repeats x 4 configs, paired bootstrap and McNemar; sites overlap with development suite; single LLM for the main study.
Toolkit paper; live measurements are batching latency and a self-consistency calibration proxy over 6 states x 5 repeats with no ground truth. Tier context.
Held-out call split but labels fully confounded with source corpus; single run, no seeds or intervals; urgency epoch count chosen after seeing the test clips.
Bootstrap, Wilson and random-split analyses; exploratory (items used during analysis development), one prespecified full-test estimate with hashed protocol; English only, one Jev version.
Authors' WEV models; website-disjoint splits; WEV-8b candidate chosen after two test reads; 153 live tasks with wide noise; no hosted Jev comparison.
Reseller's own data; one day of runs, one Jev version; cutoffs fitted on the 741 gold rows; gold is behavioural (quotes) and the fulfillment gold heuristic is unvalidated; Wilson intervals reported.
Model release README; only an in-house dev-split accuracy/ECE that the author says is not a benchmark. Tier context.
README-only deposit; means over 5 benchmarks, full tables in an external blog post not in the deposit; latencies on different hardware/routes.

Single-author thesis preprint; calibration target undefined; text/table inconsistencies (ECE 0.0542 vs 0.0546) and identical t = 24.85 across rows; LLM tiers modelled analytically; extraordinary Sharpe.
External validation set (22 reviews, 142,504 records) with a threshold fixed in advance; review-level IQRs but no CIs; comparator values copied from the TITAN-SR paper, not rerun.

Dev-selected thresholds with separate test, but the public test had been observed before the protocol was locked; mixed human/automatic labels; adaptation campaign incomplete (10 of 32 cells missing).
13-slide report; threshold and instructions set on the first 1,000 names, all metrics on the other 4,000; single run on 19 Sep 2026; 95% intervals per probability band and exact McNemar test.
Descriptive bibliometric panel; the only validation is 88 agent-adjudicated records (not human ground truth); no intervals.
Yway is the author's own Burmese model; splits by whole article and unseen test wordings; labels from Gemma 3 27B and an AI judge, not checked by native speakers; Wikipedia text only; no intervals.

Jev is the sole automated judge, one call per relation, no human validation, so its accuracy is unknown; Wilson CIs on verdict shares; analysis exploratory and not preregistered; Jev version not reported in the paper or the deposit notebook (the screening note's jev-1.13.0 could not be confirmed).

Context tier. Reuses the 492 Laya observations of Z-23065532 (same author); only the IRP correlations and the Gemini IRP evaluators are new, and neither measures the typed model. Proprietary IRP method; no intervals. The same results were posted at aiscanlab.com on 2026-09-27 (article:published_time 2026-09-27T22:56:36Z), inside the main window.
Position paper on behavioural anti-cheat built on calibrated decision models with human confirmation of bans; the abstract states that the design has not been implemented or evaluated.
Author fine-tuned Laya; 20 synthetic replications x 3 seeds plus CIC-IDS2017 with block-bootstrap CIs; response layer evaluated only in simulation; CIC-IDS2017 labels have known errors.

Dated pre-registration notes in the repository for the wording test and the dataset predictions; several analyses marked post hoc (uniform baseline, isotonic repair, clipping sensitivity; App. B); 6,844 Jev calls with a separately collected holdout; 4 Oct re-check reproduced the headline numbers; open checkpoints tested off-distribution without fine-tuning.

Authors' own open model. The sealed set was also used to compare development runs and to choose the release (a development-test set); 56-item held-out multi-step split; seed-aware intervals for four configurations, single seeds otherwise; no external baseline; calibration reported after temperature scaling. Under the §3.5 rule that requires an independently built system this is moderate.

Excluded: no evaluation of a typed decision model. The 'typed supervisor' is never identified; Table 6 runs the 'typed decision' through the same API path as gemini-flash-latest (mean 3,387 ms), consistent with a schema-constrained generative model. 90 trajectories from 30 synthetic records; descriptive metrics only; IRP proprietary. The same results were posted at aiscanlab.com on 2026-09-28 (02:08 UTC).

Author-built governance shell around hosted Jev; two live calls, one per fixture, no repeatability sweep; raw evidence JSON not published (hashes only); docs dated 2026-09-26 to 10-02, first Zenodo version 10-06.

Authors built and evaluate the supervisor around hosted Jev; 90 held-out tasks disjoint from 10 development tasks; one unseeded candidate per task-condition cell; 69-71 analysable pairs; shadow contrast post hoc; per-cell outcomes and code not released; Jev version not reported.

Zero-shot benchmark with seven hypotheses written before the main runs (App. B); prompts set on a few test games before the puzzles were generated (the author states there is no separate held-out set); one game per puzzle while Jev is non-deterministic (probabilities differ by up to 0.14 across three calls); bootstrap intervals cover puzzle choice only.

Authors' own open model trained with Kev; dated hypothesis log with failed hypotheses reported; reference sets are a consensus of two AI assistants with human spot checks, not human labels; one CI (H1), other results without intervals; release model chosen although H15 failed.
